question: How is the Colorado Real Estate Commission made up?
optionA: Three brokers and two public members
optionB: Four brokers and one public member
optionC: Five brokers and no public members
optionD: Two brokers and three public members
explanation: C.R.S. 12-10-206(1) creates a five-member commission of three brokers with at least five years of Colorado experience, one with substantial property management experience, and two members of the public. It is not an all-broker board.

question: After a Colorado broker license is revoked, when may the commission consider a new application from that person?
explanation: HB26-1287, effective August 12, 2026, amended C.R.S. 12-10-217(9) so an application from a revoked licensee is not considered until two years after revocation. One year was the waiting period before that amendment.

question: How many total hours of prelicense education must a new Colorado broker applicant complete?
explanation: C.R.S. 12-10-203(4)(a) requires 48 hours of law and practice, 48 hours of Colorado contracts and 72 hours of trust accounts, closings, legal issues and practical applications, for 168 hours. The 96-hour figure leaves out the 72-hour block.

question: A passing score on one part of the Colorado broker exam remains valid for:
explanation: Rule 2.2.E makes a passing score on either part valid for one year, and C.R.S. 12-10-212(2) cancels the exam if no application is filed within one year. Three years is the length of a renewed license cycle, not of a test score.

question: A broker's first Colorado license is issued in March. When does it expire?
optionD: Last day of March three years later
explanation: Under C.R.S. 12-10-212(4)(a)(I) and Rule 2.16.B an initial license expires at midnight on December 31 of the year it was issued. Later renewals run for three years, which is the tempting wrong answer.

question: Which Colorado broker is excused from carrying errors and omissions insurance?
explanation: C.R.S. 12-10-204(1) requires every licensee to carry errors and omissions coverage except an inactive broker or an attorney licensee with qualifying malpractice coverage. New and independent brokers who are active must be insured.

question: Besides two years of active licensure, what must a Colorado broker complete before employing other brokers?
explanation: C.R.S. 12-10-203(5)(c)(II) and Rule 2.5 require a 24-hour brokerage administration course, plus experience shown under the rule's point system. The 48-hour contracts course is part of prelicense education.

question: All Colorado broker advertising must be done clearly and conspicuously in the name of the:
explanation: Rule 6.10.A.3 requires all advertising to be in the name of the broker's brokerage firm. The only exception is a broker advertising their own property that is not listed with their firm.

question: Which word may a Colorado real estate team not use in its team name?
explanation: Rule 6.10.B.1 bars team names using Realty, Real estate, Realtors, Company, Corp., Inc., LLC, LP or other terms implying a separate entity from the brokerage. Words like Group do not imply a separate firm.

question: After a listing contract expires, how soon must the broker remove it from electronic media the broker controls?
explanation: Colorado Rule 6.10.D.2 gives the broker three days to remove an expired listing from electronic media the broker or firm controls. Under Rule 6.10.D.3, the broker also has three days to ask third-party syndicators in writing to remove the listing.

question: When a Colorado broker advertises a home's square footage, the source of that figure must be disclosed on:
explanation: Rule 6.11 requires the broker to disclose the source of the living-area square footage on the Commission-approved form. The assessor's record may be the source, but it is not the disclosure.

question: A broker prepares a market analysis for an owner's estate planning. The broker must include a notice that it:
optionA: Is valid for six months from its date
optionB: Must first be reviewed by a state-certified appraiser
optionC: Is not an appraisal and cannot be used for financing
optionD: Binds the broker to that listing price
explanation: Rule 6.12 requires a CMA or BPO prepared for any purpose other than a sale or purchase to state it is not an appraisal and cannot be used to obtain financing. Brokers may not prepare them for financing at all.

question: The seller's broker cannot be reached despite reasonable attempts. Who should receive the buyer's offer next?
explanation: Rule 6.13 sends the offer to the listing broker's employing broker when the listing broker cannot be reached. Only if that also fails, or there is no employing broker, may the offer go directly to the seller.

question: An owner with an unexpired exclusive listing calls another broker on their own. That broker may:
optionA: Take a listing that starts when the current one ends
optionB: Take an immediate listing if the owner pays a higher fee
optionC: Refuse to discuss any future listing
optionD: Cancel the current listing for the owner
explanation: Rule 6.15.B lets a broker contacted by the owner negotiate a future listing that starts when the existing exclusive listing expires or ends. The broker must advise the owner to see an attorney about ending the current listing.

question: A Colorado broker buys a duplex for personal investment. The broker must disclose being licensed:
optionA: Only if the seller asks about it
optionD: In the contract or a concurrent writing
explanation: Rule 6.17.B requires a broker buying, selling or leasing on their own account to disclose licensed status in the contracting instrument or a separate concurrent writing. Waiting for the seller to ask does not satisfy the rule.

question: Since August 2026, when must a licensee disclose an affiliated business arrangement to the party the licensee represents?
optionA: When the offer is fully executed
optionB: At the time of making the referral
explanation: HB26-1287 amended C.R.S. 12-10-218(2)(b) to require the written disclosure to the represented party at the time of the referral. Before that amendment the disclosure came when the offer was fully executed.

question: A Colorado broker may share a commission on a cooperative sale with a:
optionC: Mortgage lender who sent the buyer
optionD: Home inspector who found a client
explanation: C.R.S. 12-10-217(1)(l) forbids paying unlicensed persons for brokerage functions but allows a finder's fee or commission share with a broker licensed in another state or country. Paying a lender for a referral would also raise RESPA problems.

question: An unlicensed on-site manager supervised by a Colorado employing broker may not:
optionB: Collect rents and security deposits from tenants
optionC: Negotiate the material terms of a lease
optionD: Quote rents set by the owner
explanation: Rule 1.62 lets an unlicensed on-site manager show units, quote rents and collect money, and Rule 6.3.E.5 requires the employing broker to instruct the manager not to negotiate material lease terms.

question: In Colorado, unless a written single agency agreement exists, a broker working with a buyer is considered a:
explanation: C.R.S. 12-10-403(2) makes a broker a transaction-broker unless single agency is established by written agreement. Many states presume agency instead, which is why buyer's agent is tempting.

question: Under Colorado law, a broker may establish dual agency with a seller and a buyer:
optionA: With written consent of all parties
explanation: C.R.S. 12-10-406 states that a broker shall not establish dual agency with any seller, landlord, buyer or tenant. Written consent permits dual agency in many other states, but not in Colorado.

question: Two designated brokers in one firm act as single agents for opposite sides of one sale. This:
optionA: Creates dual agency for the whole firm
optionB: Requires both brokers to switch to transaction-broker status
optionD: Does not create dual agency for the employing broker
explanation: C.R.S. 12-10-403(6)(c) lets designated brokers act as single agents on opposite sides without creating dual agency for the employing broker or other brokers in the firm.

question: One Colorado broker works with both the seller and the buyer in one sale. Which role is not allowed?
optionC: Seller's agent with buyer as customer
optionD: Buyer's agent with seller as customer
explanation: C.R.S. 12-10-403(6)(d) and Rule 6.7 allow a broker on both sides to act as transaction-broker for both, or as single agent for one while treating the other as a customer, but never as single agent for both.

question: A seller's agent becomes a transaction-broker for both parties. The Change of Status form is due no later than:
optionC: When the consumer signs the contract
explanation: Rule 6.9 requires the Commission-approved Change of Status form when the broker begins assisting both parties, but not later than when the consumer signs the real estate contract. Closing is too late.

question: A Colorado broker must provide the written brokerage relationship disclosure before:
optionA: Eliciting confidential information from the consumer
optionB: Answering general questions about advertised listing prices
explanation: Rule 6.5 requires the C.R.S. 12-10-408 disclosures before eliciting or discussing confidential information. Small talk about styles, market conditions or advertised prices does not trigger it.

question: A buyer asks a seller's agent whether a suicide occurred in the home. Without the seller's consent, the agent:
optionB: Must disclose it as a material fact
explanation: C.R.S. 12-10-404(2)(e) bars a seller's agent from disclosing facts that may psychologically stigmatize the property without the seller's consent, and C.R.S. 38-35.5-101 says such facts are not material.

question: A Colorado buyer's agent must disclose to the seller known adverse facts about the buyer's:
optionA: Willingness to pay more than offered
optionC: Intent to occupy as a principal residence
explanation: C.R.S. 12-10-405(3)(a) requires disclosure of adverse facts about the buyer's financial ability to perform and intent to occupy. The other three are confidential under C.R.S. 12-10-405(2) without the buyer's consent.

question: A buyer agency agreement has no expiration date and no purchase ever closes. The relationship ends:
optionD: Only when a party ends it in writing
explanation: C.R.S. 12-10-409(1)(b) ends an unperformed relationship at the earliest of the agreed expiration, termination by the parties, or one year after the engagement.

question: A designated broker acting as a seller's agent may cooperate with other brokers but may not:
explanation: C.R.S. 12-10-404(5) bars a designated broker acting as seller's agent from creating subagents. C.R.S. 12-10-404(4) allows showing and listing competing properties, and 12-10-410(3) allows sharing compensation.

question: Before proposing to split the seller-paid commission, a Colorado buyer's agent must first obtain the:
explanation: C.R.S. 12-10-410(5) requires a buyer's or tenant's agent to get the client's written approval before proposing to be paid by sharing compensation from the seller or landlord.

question: Sales earnest money held by a Colorado brokerage must be deposited in its trust account within:
explanation: Rule 5.7.B sets three business days after receipt or mutual execution of the contract, whichever is later, for money other than property management funds. Five business days applies to property management money under Rule 5.7.A.

question: A Colorado brokerage that manages rentals must keep at least one separate trust account for each of:
explanation: Rule 5.5 requires a minimum of one trust account for rental receipts and one for security deposits. Commissions belong to the firm and may not sit in trust once earned.

question: How often must a Colorado brokerage complete a three-way reconciliation of a trust account holding others' money?
explanation: Rule 5.14.C requires a monthly three-way reconciliation showing the journal balance, the total of all ledgers and the reconciled bank balance agree on the same date.

question: For how long must Colorado brokers keep transaction files?
explanation: Rule 6.20 and C.R.S. 12-10-217(1)(k) require keeping transaction records for four years from consummation, or from the expiration of a listing that never closed.

question: Money in a trust account that becomes due and payable to the brokerage must be withdrawn:
explanation: Rule 5.10.A requires earned money due to the brokerage to be withdrawn monthly, so the firm's money is not commingled with funds belonging to others.

question: In a Colorado sale, who is responsible for the proper closing of the transaction for a buyer or seller?
explanation: Rule 6.19.A, under C.R.S. 12-10-217(1)(j), makes the broker for the client responsible for the proper closing, even when a title company performs the settlement.

question: A Colorado broker must make sure the client receives a closing statement that is accurate, complete and:
explanation: Rule 6.19.A requires the client to receive an accurate, complete and detailed closing statement signed by the broker. Closing statements are not recorded or approved by the Commission.

question: A broker cannot attend closing, so the firm sends another broker. The substitute broker:
optionA: Has no responsibility for the statement
optionB: Becomes the client's new single agent
optionC: Shares responsibility for the statement's accuracy
explanation: Rule 6.19.C lets a broker designated by the firm review and attend closing for the absent broker, and that broker assumes joint responsibility for accuracy, completeness and delivery of the signed statement.

question: Under Colorado's good funds law, closing funds may be disbursed when the deposit was made by:
explanation: C.R.S. 38-35-125 lets settlement agents disburse only funds available for immediate withdrawal as a matter of right, which include certified, cashier's and teller's checks. SB25-016 narrowed which wire transfers qualify but kept cashier's checks.

question: A broker completes the Commission-approved contract for the buyer. What may the broker charge for preparing it?
optionC: Fee shared with the title company
explanation: Rule 6.14.B says a broker who prepares a standard form may not charge a separate fee for that preparation. Disclosing a fee in advance does not make it allowed.

question: A Colorado broker who closes a sale charges separately for costs unrelated to form preparation. The broker must:
optionA: Fold the costs into the commission
optionB: Itemize the costs and get the parties' written consent
optionC: File the costs with the Commission before any closing
optionD: Collect the costs before the contract
explanation: Rule 6.14.B requires a broker who closes and charges separately for closing costs not related to standard forms to specify the costs and obtain the written consent of the parties charged.

question: A new associate broker with under two years of experience has a closing. The employing broker must ensure that:
optionA: Title officer reviews the commission split
optionB: Experienced broker attends or is available
explanation: Rule 6.3.D.6 requires the employing broker or an associate with more than two years of active licensure to attend closings with a new associate broker or be available for help.

question: When a Colorado brokerage transfers earnest money to the closing company, it must obtain:
explanation: Rule 5.12.B allows the transfer to the closing entity but requires a dated and signed receipt from the person or entity providing settlement services.

question: After closing, a broker working under an employing broker must deliver the closing statements to the:
explanation: Rule 6.19.A requires a broker licensed with a firm to deliver the closing statements and other closing documents to the brokerage firm immediately following closing, for the file and supervision.

question: Which is a protected class under Colorado fair housing law but not under the federal Fair Housing Act?
explanation: C.R.S. 24-34-502(1)(a) adds marital status, among others, to the federal classes. Familial status, national origin and disability are already protected federally.

question: Colorado law bars a landlord from refusing to rent because of a person's lawful, verifiable:
explanation: C.R.S. 24-34-502(1)(l) makes it an unfair housing practice to refuse to rent because of source of income, defined in 24-34-501(4.5) to include public housing assistance. Pets and smoking are not protected classes.

question: Under the Colorado Foreclosure Protection Act, a homeowner may cancel a foreclosure consulting contract:
explanation: C.R.S. 6-1-1105(1) gives the homeowner the right to cancel a foreclosure consulting contract at any time, in addition to any other rescission right. Three business days is a common federal rescission period.

question: Under the Colorado Foreclosure Protection Act, a foreclosure consultant may collect compensation only:
optionB: Once the sale date is postponed
optionC: After fully performing every promised service
optionD: After the notice of election and demand is recorded
explanation: C.R.S. 6-1-1107(1)(a) bars a consultant from collecting compensation until every service contracted for or promised has been fully performed. Payment at signing is exactly what the law prohibits.

question: A Colorado home sells for $450,000. What state documentary fee is due on the deed?
explanation: C.R.S. 39-13-102(2)(b) sets the fee at one cent per $100 of consideration over $500: $450,000 / 100 = 4,500 x $0.01 = $45.00. The $450.00 answer uses ten cents per $100.

question: When Colorado withholding applies to a nonresident seller on a sale over $100,000, the amount withheld is:
optionA: 2% of the price or net proceeds, if less
explanation: C.R.S. 39-22-604.5 requires the closing agent to withhold 2 percent of the sales price or the net proceeds, whichever is less; sales of $100,000 or less are exempt. 15 percent is the federal FIRPTA rate for foreign sellers.

question: A Colorado owner pays property taxes in two equal installments. The second installment is due by:
explanation: C.R.S. 39-10-104.5(2) sets the first installment by the last day of February and the second by June 15. The last day of April is the deadline for paying the full amount in one payment.

question: Which type of form must a Colorado broker use when an appropriate one exists for the transaction?
explanation: C.R.S. 12-10-403(4)(c) and Rule 7.1.A require a Commission-approved form whenever one exists and is appropriate. Attorney and Bar Association forms are allowed only when no suitable Commission form exists.

question: An attorney form used by a Colorado broker must name its drafter and state that it:
optionA: Has been reviewed and accepted by the Colorado Division of Real Estate
optionB: Is binding only after it is recorded
optionD: Has not been approved by the Colorado Real Estate Commission
explanation: Rule 7.1.B requires an attorney form to say it has not been approved by the Colorado Real Estate Commission and to name the attorney or law firm and the broker or firm it was prepared for.

question: A Colorado broker may use a form drafted by the brokerage's attorney only when:
optionD: Closing will be handled by an attorney
explanation: Rule 7.1.B allows an attorney form only if a Commission-approved form does not exist or is not appropriate, and the broker may change it only by completing blanks.

question: A client gives their broker a contract form of the client's own to use. The broker must:
optionA: Rewrite it on a Commission form first
optionB: Send it to the Commission for approval
optionC: Refuse to use it unless a Colorado attorney drafted it
optionD: Keep written confirmation that the client supplied it
explanation: Rule 7.1.C and C.R.S. 12-10-403(4)(b)(III) allow a client form if the broker retains written confirmation that the party provided it, and the broker may only insert transaction-specific information.

question: A letter of intent prepared by a Colorado broker must state on its face that it:
optionA: Is nonbinding and creates no legal rights
optionB: Expires ten calendar days after signing
optionC: Was drafted by a licensed Colorado attorney
explanation: Rule 7.1.H and C.R.S. 12-10-403(4)(b)(VIII) require a broker's letter of intent to state that it is nonbinding and creates no legal rights or obligations, and to note it is not Commission-approved.

question: A broker deletes a section of a Commission contract that does not apply. The caption must stay, followed by:
explanation: Rule 7.2.F lets a broker delete listed sections that do not apply, but the caption must remain unaltered and be followed by the words omitted-not applicable.

question: Deletions or changes to the printed body of a Commission-approved form must:
optionA: Have the employing broker's written approval first
optionB: Appear only in a separate addendum
optionD: Result from negotiation or a party's instruction
explanation: Rule 7.2.C requires any deletion or modification of the printed body to result from negotiations or a party's instructions, with deleted text struck through so it stays legible.

question: Words a broker inserts into blanks on a Commission-approved form must be:
optionA: In a clearly different font style
explanation: Rule 7.2.E requires inserted provisions to be in a font style or type that clearly differs from the Commission-approved form language, so readers can tell what was added.

question: A broker who is not a party adds a clause limiting the brokerage's liability to a standard form. This is:
optionA: Allowed if both parties initial it
explanation: Rule 7.4.B bars a broker who is not a principal party from inserting personal provisions, disclaimers or exculpatory language favoring the broker or firm into a standard form.

question: When completing standard forms, a Colorado broker must advise the parties that the forms:
optionB: Cannot be changed by the parties
optionD: Must be recorded to be valid
explanation: C.R.S. 12-10-403(4)(c) and Rule 7.1 require the broker to advise the parties that the forms have important legal consequences and that they should consult legal counsel before signing.

question: A transaction-specific clause drafted by the brokerage's Colorado attorney must be kept by the broker for:
optionC: Four years after its last use
explanation: Rule 7.3.B requires the broker to retain attorney-drafted clauses for four years from the date the clause was last used and to provide them, with the attorney's name, on Commission request.

question: Every Colorado contract for residential property must contain a bold-faced disclosure about:
explanation: C.R.S. 38-35.7-101 requires every residential purchase contract to warn that special taxing districts may carry general obligation debt that can raise mill levies. The seller bears the duty to give it.

question: The required disclosure for a home in a common interest community warns that unpaid assessments may result in:
explanation: C.R.S. 38-35.7-102 requires the contract to state that an unpaid assessment can lead the association to place a lien on the property and possibly sell it to pay the debt.

question: If a Colorado home's potable water comes from a well, the seller's disclosure must include:
optionB: Copy of the current well permit, if available
optionD: Letter of approval from the county health department
explanation: C.R.S. 38-35.7-104(1)(b) requires the seller to provide a copy of the current well permit, if one is available, when the disclosed water source is a well.

question: A buyer's test shows an unremediated meth lab, and the seller receives written notice. The seller may retest within:
explanation: C.R.S. 38-35.7-103(2)(b) gives the seller thirty days after the notice for a second independent test. Ninety days is the time a buyer who assumes liability has to remediate after closing.

question: A seller knew of past meth production and did not disclose it. The buyer's suit must start within:
explanation: C.R.S. 38-35.7-103(3)(c) requires the buyer to commence the action within three years after the date the purchase closed. Eighteen years is Colorado's adverse possession period.

question: Colorado's required oil and gas disclosure warns a buyer that the surface estate:
optionA: May be owned apart from the minerals below
optionC: Cannot be entered by mineral owners
optionD: Is assessed and taxed together with the minerals
explanation: C.R.S. 38-35.7-108 requires notice that the surface may be owned separately from the minerals and that mineral owners or lessees may enter and use the surface to reach them.

question: Under Colorado law, a deed of trust securing a home loan is treated as a:
optionA: Conveyance of legal title to the lender
optionB: Conveyance of title to the public trustee
optionC: Lease of the property to the borrower
optionD: Lien, not a conveyance of title
explanation: C.R.S. 38-35-117 provides that mortgages and trust deeds are not conveyances, so the lender cannot take possession without foreclosure and sale. Colorado is a lien-theory state.

question: A public trustee sale of nonagricultural property is first set how long after the notice of election is recorded?
explanation: C.R.S. 38-38-108(1)(a) sets the initial public trustee sale 110 to 125 calendar days after recording the notice of election and demand. The 215 to 230 day window applies to agricultural property.

question: To cure a monetary foreclosure default, the owner must file a notice of intent to cure no later than:
explanation: C.R.S. 38-38-104(1) requires the notice of intent to cure to be filed with the officer no later than fifteen calendar days before the sale. Eight business days after the sale is a junior lienor's deadline to file intent to redeem.

question: Colorado land is deeded to Ann and Bob with no wording about the form of ownership. They hold title as:
explanation: C.R.S. 38-31-101 creates joint tenancy only when the deed declares it, such as 'in joint tenancy'; any other conveyance to two or more persons creates a tenancy in common. Colorado has neither tenancy by the entirety nor community property.

question: In Colorado, how many years of adverse possession is conclusive evidence of absolute ownership?
explanation: C.R.S. 38-41-101(1) sets an eighteen-year limitation and makes eighteen years of adverse possession conclusive evidence of ownership. It does not run against the state or local governments.
